title: Economic model for longevity interventions
bottleneck: The pharmaceutical business model requires clear disease endpoints and billion-dollar markets, but longevity interventions target aging itself, which regulators do not recognize as an indication. The result: geroscience companies must contort into narrow disease indications to get funded, distorting the science toward whatever is reimbursable rather than what slows aging.
why_it_blocks: The science of aging is moving faster than the economic machinery to translate it. Without a viable business and regulatory model, the best biology stays trapped in papers instead of becoming prescriptions.
current_state: No drug is approved for an aging indication. The TAME trial seeks to establish one; longevity biotech funding remains a fraction of oncology or immunology despite the larger addressable burden. Some funds now pursue longevity biotech as an asset class, but without an FDA-recognized aging indication, exits depend on repurposing candidates into conventional disease labels.
